body-secondary.note: Translucent Ink rather than a gray; a solid gray in its place reads visibly cooler.

control-border.note: Translucent so a control edge darkens with whatever it sits on rather than fighting it.

legacy-primary.note: Pre-Tailwind Bootstrap blue. Survives on the checked checkbox only; not for new work.

headline.purpose: Page and major section titles in routine use.

body.purpose: Prose, form values, dialog text. The least-used role in a system made of tables.

data.purpose: The numeric readout: table cells, card values, the right-aligned figure in a mobile row. Weight 600 is what separates a value from its label.

label.purpose: Table column headers and mobile card field names. Uppercase plus 0.05em tracking plus Muted Ink is the system most recognizable typographic gesture.

scale.purpose: Every literal font size the UI actually renders, from the 0.5rem legend glyph to the 2.5rem h1 endpoint. A record of what exists, not a menu to pick from; new work picks a role.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Cards and the desktop table wrapper. Barely visible; its job is to keep white-on-white from vibrating.

shadows.name: shadow-control
shadows.purpose: Buttons and ghost controls. Inverted to inset on press so the button reads as depressed rather than moved.

shadows.name: shadow-lifted
shadows.purpose: Mobile card hover and the dropdown menu. The strongest shadow in routine use.

shadows.name: shadow-nav
shadows.purpose: The sticky navbar at 992px and up, when the bar is actually overlapping scrolled content.

shadows.name: shadow-overlay
shadows.purpose: Toasts. The only shadow allowed to be seen from across the room, because a toast has to arrive.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for every state transition in the system.

motion.name: transition-fast
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, and color transitions on controls, nav links, and mobile cards.

motion.name: transition-base
motion.purpose: Sort indicator opacity and the add-new button.

motion.name: transition-slow
motion.purpose: The nav indicator scaleX and the route fade-slide (20px translateY).

motion.name: transition-chip
motion.purpose: Filter chips, dialog buttons, and table row action buttons only, on plain ease. A faster tier that makes filtering feel immediate.

motion.name: value-flash
motion.purpose: The gain/loss background pulse when a price changes, peaking at 20% alpha. Exempt from prefers-reduced-motion because it is information.

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: Button and page spinners. Kept running under prefers-reduced-motion so a working control still reads as working.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.note: The signature switch: data tables become mobile card stacks below this.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.note: Navigation becomes sticky and picks up shadow-nav.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.note: Fluid heading ramp stops growing and locks to fixed sizes.

breakpoints.name: 2xl
breakpoints.note: Declared token; no layout change hangs off it.

breakpoints.name: ad-hoc-389
breakpoints.note: Small-phone compaction tier for mobile card padding and value size.

breakpoints.name: ad-hoc-666
breakpoints.note: Data table collapses to data-label prefixed blocks.

breakpoints.name: ad-hoc-844
breakpoints.note: Tablet band: icon-plus-label buttons tighten so action rows do not wrap.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action on a screen. The 135deg gradient reverses on hover rather than lightening.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; color: #fff; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4361ee 0%, #3651d4 100%); border: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.04); cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #3651d4 0%, #4361ee 100%); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.04); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgb(67 97 238 / 0.4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The workhorse action. A 2% black tint with a hairline border, visible at rest unlike a true ghost button; hover is the only place the accent appears. Adjacent ghost buttons are spaced 0.375rem apart, never joined.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: #6c757d; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.02); border: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); border-radius: 0.375rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.04); cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-ghost + .ds-btn-ghost { margin-left: 0.375rem; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #4361ee; background-color: rgb(67 97 238 / 0.08); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgb(67 97 238 / 0.4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Platform Filter Chip
components.description: Broker filter toggles. Active fills Control Graphite, never the accent: a filter being on is a fact, not an event. Runs on the fast 120ms tier.
components.css: .ds-chip-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; } .ds-chip { font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; color: #6b7280; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 0.375rem; padding: 0.3125rem 0.625rem; cursor: pointer; transition: all 120ms ease; } .ds-chip:hover { color: #4b5563; background: #f8fafc; border-color: #cbd5e1; } .ds-chip:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-chip--active { color: #fff; background: #4b5563; border-color: #4b5563; } .ds-chip-sep { width: 1px; height: 1.25rem; background: #d1d5db; }

components.name: Dialog Button
components.description: Confirmation dialogs use their own quieter vocabulary so a decision reads as a control panel choice, not a marketing call to action. Confirm fills graphite; destructive confirm fills Loss Red.
components.css: .ds-dialog-actions { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 1rem; border-top: 1px solid #dee2e6; } .ds-dialog-btn { font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: #6b7280; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 0.375rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; cursor: pointer; transition: all 120ms ease; } .ds-dialog-btn:hover { color: #4b5563; background: #f8fafc; border-color: #cbd5e1; } .ds-dialog-btn:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-dialog-btn--primary { color: #fff; background: #4b5563; border-color: #4b5563; } .ds-dialog-btn--primary:hover { color: #fff; background: #374151; border-color: #374151; } .ds-dialog-btn--danger { color: #fff; background: #dc3545; border-color: #dc3545; } .ds-dialog-btn--danger:hover { color: #fff; background: #c82333; border-color: #c82333; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Surface Subtle fill so a field never disappears into the card behind it. Focus outlines, it does not glow.
components.css: .ds-field { display: block; font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { display: block; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6b7280; } .ds-input { width: 100%; font-family: inherit; font-size: 1rem; color: #212529; background-color: #fcfcfd; border: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; transition: border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #4361ee; outline: 2px solid rgb(67 97 238 / 0.2); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-input.is-invalid { border-color: #dc3545; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: The one place the accent marks position. Active goes bold plus a 2px indigo underline that scales in from zero at 300ms; hover previews the same indicator.
components.html: Instruments Transactions
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.5rem 0; background: #fff; border-bottom: 1px solid #dee2e6; } .ds-nav-link { position: relative; font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; color: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.65); text-decoration: none; padding: 0.5rem; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link--active { color: #4361ee; } .ds-nav-link--active { font-weight: bold; } .ds-nav-indicator { position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: -0.125rem; left: 0; height: 0.125rem; background-color: #4361ee; transform: scaleX(0); transition: transform 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover .ds-nav-indicator, .ds-nav-link--active .ds-nav-indicator { transform: scaleX(1); }

components.css: .ds-table-wrap { overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid #dee2e6; border-radius: 0.5rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); } .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-table th, .ds-table td { padding: 1rem 0.75rem; background-color: #fcfcfd; border-bottom: 1px solid #dee2e6; vertical-align: middle; text-align: left; } .ds-table thead th { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6b7280; border-bottom: 2px solid #e9ecef; } .ds-table tbody tr:hover td { background-color: rgb(67 97 238 / 0.02); } .ds-num { text-align: right; font-weight: 600; } .ds-gain { color: #21c55d; } .ds-loss { color: #dc3545; }

components.css: .ds-mcard { overflow: hidden; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; padding: 1rem; font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #e9ecef; border-radius: 0.5rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-mcard:hover { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08); } .ds-mcard-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.5rem 0; } .ds-mcard-row:not(:last-child) { border-bottom: 1px solid #f8f9fa; } .ds-mcard-row:first-child { padding-top: 0; } .ds-mcard-row:last-child { padding-bottom: 0; } .ds-mcard-label { flex: 0 0 auto; min-width: 80px; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; color: #6c757d; } .ds-mcard-value { flex: 1; text-align: right; font-weight: 600; word-break: break-word; } .ds-mcard-gain { color: #21c55d; }

components.name: Value Flash
components.description: The only ambient motion in the product. A 3s wash peaking at 20% alpha of the exact semantic Gain Green or Loss Red, deliberately exempt from prefers-reduced-motion because it is information, not decoration.
components.css: @keyframes ds-pulse-increase { 0% { background-color: transparent; } 50% { background-color: rgb(33 197 93 / 0.2); } 100% { background-color: transparent; } } @keyframes ds-pulse-decrease { 0% { background-color: transparent; } 50% { background-color: rgb(220 53 69 / 0.2); } 100% { background-color: transparent; } } .ds-flash-up { animation: ds-pulse-increase 3s ease-in-out; transition: background-color 3s ease-in-out; } .ds-flash-down { animation: ds-pulse-decrease 3s ease-in-out; transition: background-color 3s ease-in-out; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-flash-up, .ds-flash-down { animation-duration: 3s !important; } }

components.name: Toast
components.description: Fixed-width panels pinned top right, driven by a single --toast-bg custom property. The container is pointer-events: none so a toast never blocks the page beneath.
components.css: .ds-toast-container { position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; z-index: 1090; padding: 1rem; pointer-events: none; } .ds-toast-container > :not(:last-child) { margin-bottom: 1.5rem; } .ds-toast { --toast-bg: #4b5563; width: 350px; font-family: Avenir, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #fff; background-color: var(--toast-bg); border-radius: 0.375rem; box-shadow: 0 0.5rem 1rem rgb(0 0 0 / 0.15); } .ds-toast--success { --toast-bg: #28a745; } .ds-toast--info { --toast-bg: #17a2b8; } .ds-toast--error { --toast-bg: #dc3545; } .ds-toast--warning { --toast-bg: #ffc107; } .ds-toast-body { padding: 0.75rem; }

narrative.overview: The domain's own word for the things this app tracks is instrument, and the interface takes that literally. A panel of calibrated readouts: the chrome is quiet, machined, and gets out of the way; the values are the only things allowed to be loud. Nothing on screen is decorative. Every saturated pixel is either a number's sign, the position you're currently in, or something asking to be pressed. When a price actually moves, the cell it lives in glows for three seconds and then goes back to being furniture: the one moment of animation in the system is a readout confirming it changed, not a flourish.
keyCharacteristics: Hairline-bordered, near-flat surfaces; shadow reserved for genuine float
High density, small type (12-14px dominant), weight over size for hierarchy
One reserved accent (Signal Indigo) for navigation and primary action; neutral graphite for everything else that is merely on
Green and red mean gain and loss and nothing else
Motion only confirms a state change; the reduced-motion path keeps only the spinner and the price flash
Tables on desktop become label/value cards under 767px: the signature responsive move

rules.name: The Reserved Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Indigo is spent on exactly three things: where you are (nav), what you are focused on (focus ring), and the one primary action on the screen. Anything that is merely selected, active, or toggled uses Control Graphite. If a screen has two indigo elements competing for "primary", one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Signed-Number Rule
rules.body: Green and red are reserved for the sign of a value and for destructive intent. Never use them for status chips, category badges, brand accent, or emphasis. A red pixel on this interface means "you lost money" or "this will delete something", and it must never mean anything else.

rules.name: The Single-Source Rule
rules.body: Every color in the system is declared once, in the @theme static block of ui/styles/theme.css, and consumed as var(--color-*) or as a Tailwind utility derived from it. There is no second palette layer to reconcile against. A hardcoded near-miss hex in a component (#ef4444 beside Loss Red, #0d6efd beside Signal Indigo) is not a shortcut, it is a fork; the four sites that still do it are drift, not precedent.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by weight (500 to 600 to 700) and color, not by scale. The gap between a label and its value is 100 weight units and one color step, not four points of size. Reaching for a larger font to create emphasis breaks the density the tables depend on.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Numeric columns must set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. It is set once, on body in the base layer, and inherits everywhere, which is exactly how it should stay. Any component that introduces its own font-variant-numeric (or a font stack without tabular figures) breaks the alignment of every right-aligned money column beneath it.

rules.name: The Documented-Step Rule
rules.body: A font size that is not already in typography.scale does not get added by writing it in a component. Either it maps to one of the five roles, or the ramp entry lands in theme.css and in DESIGN.md first.

rules.name: The Two-Speeds Rule
rules.body: Every data surface ships two renderings of the same truth: a dense desktop table and a mobile label/value card stack. Neither is a fallback. If a new column is added to the table and not to the card, the phone view has silently lost information.

rules.name: The Hairline-First Rule
rules.body: Reach for a 1px border before a shadow. Shadow is reserved for elements that genuinely float above the page: modals, the sticky navbar, a card under the finger. A shadow used to separate two adjacent surfaces is a border that has not been written yet.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: Controls get 0.375rem; containers get 0.5rem. A container inside a container does not get a smaller radius, it gets a hairline. Introducing a third radius for a single component fragments the form language.

dos: Do reach for a 1px hairline before a shadow. If two surfaces need separating, that is a border.
Do spend Signal Indigo (#4361ee) only on navigation state, focus rings, and the single primary action. Use Control Graphite (#4b5563) for anything that is merely selected or toggled.
Do ship both renderings when adding a data column: the desktop table cell and the mobile card label/value pair.
Do carry hierarchy with weight (500 to 600 to 700) and color, not with size. Keep the type small.
Do set uppercase 0.75rem/600 with 0.05em tracking in Muted Ink for every column header and field label: it is the system most recognizable gesture.
Do add every new token to the @theme static block in ui/styles/theme.css and consume it as var(--color-*) or its Tailwind utility. That block is the only palette.
Do use outlines for focus (2px solid, 2px offset), never a glow, and never suppress the focus ring on a control that can be tabbed to.
Do let font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums inherit from body. Every money column depends on it.
Do keep skeleton placeholders shape-matched to the real content so nothing reflows on load.
Do hold the container at --container-app (min(1350px, 91vw)). The gutter is intentional at every width.
donts: Don't use green or red for anything other than the sign of a value or a destructive action. No green active chips, no red new badges.
Don't hardcode a near-miss hex. #ef4444 beside Loss Red and #0d6efd beside Signal Indigo are the existing drift, and every one of them is a color the theme already names.
Don't introduce a third font stack. Two are already declared and disagree (#app's Avenir wins over body's system stack); consolidate rather than add.
Don't add a new radius value. Controls are 0.375rem, containers are 0.5rem.
Don't add a font size that isn't already in typography.scale. The twenty-one recorded steps are a measurement of existing drift, not an invitation to widen it.
Don't re-add shadows to buttons or table wrappers beyond shadow-control and shadow-card. The flatness is the material.
Don't treat the mobile card stack as a degraded table. It is a designed rendering and it must carry every value the table carries.
Don't animate anything that isn't confirming a state change. The value flash and the spinners are the whole motion budget.

Don't put a scoped style block in a component to override a components.css rule and expect the layer order to explain it. Scoped styles are injected unlayered and therefore beat every @layer; that is why an override works and why it is invisible to anyone reading the cascade.
Don't reach for a gray-* ramp value when a semantic token names the same role. The ramp exists for the component layer's older internals, not for new work.
